question: In Rutherford's model of an atom, which of the following particles are double charged on helium ions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alpha particles**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Alpha particles** are identified as **doubly charged helium ions** because they consist of **two protons** and **two neutrons**, effectively making them a **helium nucleus (He²⁺)** without any electrons.
 
• In **1911**, the physicist **Ernest Rutherford** utilized these particles in his landmark scattering experiment to investigate the internal structure of the **atom**.
 
• Because an **alpha particle** has a mass of approximately **4 atomic mass units (u)** and a **positive charge of +2**, it was an ideal probe for interacting with the dense parts of the atom.
